KENTUCKY NEGRO IS PURSUED BY POSSEE
Brute Who Assaulted 16-Year-Old Woman Will Be Lynched If Captured; Woman In Delicate Condition
Lexington, Ky., Aug. 5.—A posse of several hundred farmers and county officers armed with guns, ropes and pitchforks this morning continued to scout Madison, Jessamine and Fayette counties in search for Buford Mondya, mulatto, 28 years of age charged with having assaulted Mrs Charles Sauers, 16 years old, of Valley View Madison county, Ky., 11 miles from here.

The posse spent yesterday and last night searching for the negro who is alleged to have forcibly entered the Sauers home and committed the assault upon Mrs. Sauers Monday evening. Yesterday afternoon Mrs. Sauers, who is about to become a mother, regained consciousness for first time since the assault and related her story. She said Monday threw a powdered drug into her face.
buford-monday-valley-view-1920-08-11.A3:
HUNT FOR NEGRO WHO ATTACKED WOMAN
Kentucky Farmers Armed With Guns,
Ropes and Pitch forks Seek
Fugitive.
Lexington, Ky., August 5. — A posse of several hundred farmers and county officers, armed with guns, ropes and pitchforks, this morning, is scouring Madison, Jessamine and Fayette counties in a search for Buford Monday, 28, mulatto, charged with having attacked Mrs. Charles Sauers, 16, of Valley View, Madison county, Ky., 15 miles from here.

The posse spent all yesterday afternoon and last night searching for the negro, who is alleged to have forcibly entered the Sauers home and attacked Mrs. Sauers Monday morning, Yesterday afternoon Mrs. Sauers, who is about to become a mother, regained consciousness for the first time since the attack upon her, and related her story. She said Monday threw a powdered drug into her face.

Monday was seen at Nicholasville, Jessamine county, late yesterday afternoon, according to members of the posse. He was formerly in the army and saw service in France.
buford-monday-valley-view-1920-08-11.A4:
BIG POSSE MAKES
MIDNIGHT HUNT
Seeking Assailant of Mrs. Robt. Sowers, of Valley View— City and Trains Searched
As a result of an assault upon Mrs. Robert Sowers, at her home home near Valley View, Tuesday night, which left her in a precarious condition, a posse of irate citizens headed by Deputy Sheriff James Taylor, of Valley View, scoured Madison as well as a large portion of Fayette county, Wednesday and Wednesday night in search of a colored man named Munday, of Valley View, who was charged with the crime after the recovery of Mrs. Sowers, more than four hours later.

The posse, which made for Lexington, where the negro was trailed, split there upon failure to find their quarry, one part coming to Richmond. This city was combed late Wednesday night and during the early hours of Thursday morning in a vain effort to locate Munday. The latter is said to have been on a Richmond bound train, which he boarded, reports declare, at Nicholasville. Munday evidently was aware that he was being sought, for when the posse searched the train near Richmond he was not aboard, and it is believed he detrained between the and Nicholasville.

The posse, after a thorough search of Richmond was completed, called at the home of Sheriff Whitlock and sought information. They stated the case, but asked for no warrant. When asked why the local authorities had not been notified, the officer was informed that the man sought had been trailed in another direction, towards Lexington, and that city was thrown into a state of unusual excitement at a late hour by the visit of the posse. While it is believed that he made his way to Lexington, the theory is advanced that he back-tracked part of the way, leaving the train between the cities, in an effort to thwart his pursuers.

Mrs. Sowers, who is a young and said to be very attractive woman, was so frightened that she was unable for more than four hours after being discovered, to explain her terrible experience. She gave the name of her alleged assailant and stated details to her husband and other relatives up until she became unconscious. A physician was sought and was in attendance most of the day Wednesday.

The feeling against her assailant is said to be very bitter at Valley View, where he had been a resident for some time. The condition of Mrs. Sowers was reported Thursday as being such as to cause her to be confined to her bed, however, the attending physician is of the belief that she will recover. Robert Sowers, her Husband, is a son of Mrs. Mollie Sowers, of Valley View.
buford-monday-valley-view-1920-08-11.A10:
WARRANT IS OUT
FOR BUFORD MONDAY
Victim At Valley View Recovering—His Arrest In Cincinnati Reported
Mr. Herman Howard, brother of Mrs. Charles Sowers, of Valley View, victim of Buford Munday, negro, the first of the week, came to Richmond Thursday evening and caused to be filed in the county court a charge of criminal assault. Howard stated that his sister and Sowers were married last Christmas, when she was 16 years old. He said her condition was improved, and asserted the reason for not notifying the local authorities was that Munday had gone in the vicinity of Lexington, and that a posse was following him, and would capture him before reaching that city, had he not been notified by friends that the posse was on his trail. Howard said his sister was looking forward to the first arrival in their little family within a period of two months, and this fact rendered her condition more serious. He said Munday had been in Richmond many times, where he had sold fish, and was known as a worthless character in many ways. He has spent the past several years about Valley View, except when in the country's service.

Howard claimed that feeling ran high and he feared that if Munday was captured he would never reach jail. Late Thursday night there were reports to the effect that the telephone lines had been cut between Richmond and Valley View. This, however, proved untrue. Early Friday morning reports reached Richmond to the effect that Munday had been apprehended in Cincinnati, but this report has not been verified, although an inquiry had been sent out at an early hour.

The Lexington Herald had the following story about the horrible crime and the search for the negro Friday morning:

Continued search by the local police department, deputies from the Fayette county sheriff's office, and a posse headed by Deputy Sheriff James Taylor of Valley View, for Buford Monday, alleged assaulter of Mrs. Charles Sowers, the young wife of a prominent Madison county farmer, has proved fruitless up to a late hour last night.

Monday, it is rumored, was seen in Lexington Wednesday night about 8 o'clock by a negro acquaintance, but the local police were unable to locate the man. A later rumor stated that the mulatto boarded the Chesapeake and Ohio train at 7:20 o'clock in the city, after purchasing a ticket for Ashland., where it is claimed he has a wife and several children. The Ashland authorities were notified at once. He has not been living with his wife for several months, according to the police.

A story from Nicholasville indicates that the mulatto evidently did not fear capture at Richmond. for it is claimed that he purchased a ticket for the Madison county capital Wednesday, two days after the crime was committed, and was in the act of boarding the train when a friend of Monday's told him that the Madison county authorities were looking for him. He bought a ticket to Lexington after this incident, the Nicholasville report continued.

Monday is well known in Lexington police circles, having been arrested in this city ten years ago on a charge of grand larceny. Chief of Police J. J. Reagan stated yesterday. His case was transferred to the Jessamine county county court at that time.

The crime occurred Monday morning. Mrs. Sowers was found lying on the floor of her home when her husband returned several hours later. Efforts to revive her proved futile, and it was not until late Wednesday afternoon that she regained consciousness. She then told her story of the assault and search for the negro began.

buford-monday-valley-view-1920-08-11.A15:
MUNDAY ROPORTED IN
PULASKI COUNTY
(Nicholasville News)

Word raeached Nicholasville Monday night that Buford Munday, the negro of Valley View, who assaulted Mrs. Charles Sowers at that place last week, has been seen near Burnside, and Harry Hughes was detailed to investigate the matter.

A good description of the negro was given the police to aid them in their search. According to those who know Munday, he was described as being a light mulatto about 5 feet and 6 inches all. He had three gold teeth on the right side of his mouth. He was wearing a blue coat and white palm peach trousers, a straw hat and tan shoes. His hair is black, thin and fine.

Munday is an ex-soldier and saw service in France during the war. He was formerly married but separated from his wife some time ago. His wife at the present time is living at Catlettsburg. Munday has a brother, who operates a restaurant in Cincinnati. He is about 28 years old. He has been operating a lunch stand at Valley View and sold sandwiches, pies, etc., when the train stopped there at noon. He frequently comes to Nicholasville and plays a guitar or a banjo when loafing. Charles Sowers, husband of the victim, is well known in that portion of Madison county near Jessamine and Fayette counties. He is a farmer.
buford-monday-valley-view-1920-08-11.A17:
SEARCH WITH GUNS FOR POLITE MAN
Lexington, Ky., Aug. 11—Because Buford Monday, colored, age 28, tipped his hat to Mrs. Charles Sauers, white, of Valley View, Madison county, she gave the alarm that he had attempted to assault her. As a result, the entire community, including police officers and citizens, are searching for Monday with pitchforks, guns, clubs, mallets, and other engines of Southern warfare, bent upon lynching him on sight.

Memphis, Tenn., Aug. 11—The 51st Annual Session of the Sunday School Convention ended in this city this week. The convention was held at Mt. Nebo Baptist Church, pastored by the Rev. A. H. Henderson. The introductory sermon at the convention was delivered by the Rev. L. Tyler. The report of the various branches of the association indicated that unusual efforts were being put forth for the success of the association.

RACE RIOT REPORTED Deputy Sheriffs Rush to Chicago Heights In Anticipa- tion of Clash. By United Press
CHICAGO, Aug. 6.—Twenty-five deputy sheriffs were rushed to Chicago Heights today on account of reported race riots there between whites and blacks. As yet no trouble has occurred between whites and negroes.

In the last three days 500 Chicago Heights whites and 3,500 negroes have left town following threats by Italians to "get even" for the murder of an Italian by a Hungarian.

When the Italians gathered at the home of a Hungarian, it was reported that they were after a negro.

NATIONAL GUARD READY
TO QUELL RACE RIOTING
Italians Drive Negroes in Droves From Chicago Heights Following Attempted Assault. [By Universal Service.]
Attempted Assault.
[By Universal Service.]

CHICAGO, August 6.—One company of the Illinois National Guard is mobilized here tonight and ready to leave on a moment's notice for Chicago heights, twenty miles from here, where rioting is reported between Italians and negroes.

Negroes are reported to be leaving the town in droves. The business portion of the town is reported quiet tonight but disturbances continued in the factory district. The guardsmen are fully armed and ammunition has been issued to them.

Fifteen deputy sheriffs were rushed to Chicago Heights today to stop the rioting if possible. It was upon word from that town that the guardsmen were called out. Disturbances have been reported all day.

Trouble started several days ago, when two negroes are reported to have attacked an Italian girl. A riot occurred at the time. The Italians are also objecting to negroes moving into white residential districts and taking the places of striking factory workers. No fatalities have been reported so far.
chicago-heights-chicago-heights-1920-08-.A4:
MILITA CALMS
RIOT FEARS AT
CHICAGO HEIGHTS
Chicago Heights breathes easier today as the belief becomes general that rioting between blacks and foreigners has been averted. Twenty-five deputy sheriffs are now patrolling the streets and Co. L. of the Illinois National Guard, a home unit is still holding itself in readiness at the Chicago Heights Armory.

Mayor E. G. Klinger announced this morning that many of the trouble makers in both parties wert leaving the village. The presence of the deputies who were rushed to Chicago Heights yesterday and the sight of members of the local militia company around their armory in uniform had a quieting ect, the mayor declared.

Because of the inactivity of the suspected disturbers last night the militia company was not detailed on the treets. The Chicago Heights company of the national guard comprises about fifty members. In the event that more help is needed, officials have planned to call on other companies in Evansen, Wilmette and Blue Island.

The company of militia is fully unformed and rifles were issued at the time of mobilization. It is thought serious trouble will be averted when the men have been assigned to patrols over the factory district.

The causes of the trouble between Italians and negroes are said to be an attempted attack on an Italian girl by two alleged men several days ago and the fact that a number of colored laborers were put in the factories as strike-breakers when a number of the Italians struck a short time ago.
chicago-heights-chicago-heights-1920-08-.A5:
CHICAGO HEIGHTS
RIOTS MINIMIZED
Chicago, Aug. 7.—The seriousness of the reported rioting at Chicago Heights yesterday was minimized today by Chief of Police Thomas Stone. He said that there had been minor clashes and street fights occurring for the last two years, and characterized yesterday's affair as mostly a matter of rumor which was given substance because of known dissatisfaction among the foreign elements of the heights on account of the presence of numbers of negro residents in the Italian and Hungarian districts.

Police Are Working On New Murder
Body of Man Believed to Be Dino Sanitelli of Gary is Found by Road-side.
With his skull crushed and three bullet wounds in his body, a man was found dying at the side of the road, two miles east of Chicago Heights last night at 11:30 o'clock.

Identification is only partly established thus far, but friends believe him to have been a Gary Italian, whose first name was Frank.

When found the man was barely able to speak and died before police could get a connected story from him. About the only words which were of value to the officers were his whispered statement that he had been shot by a negro named Taylor.

Chicago Heights police are working on the murder which is believed may have some connection with the recent trouble between negroes and Italian residents of the city.

The body was discovered huddled at the roadside having apparently been thrown from a moving automobile. The road leads from Chicago Heights to Dyer, Ind. Only meagre identification clues were found when the man's clothing was searched. In one pocket was a small card bearing the words "Hammond 1699-W." In another pocket was another card with the single word "Dino."

Hammond police were notified at once and Capt. Bunde found the number to be that of the telephone of Ed Babcock, 488 Summer street. Mrs. Babcock informed the police that her husband was at work. She was told of the murder and when the man was described as an Italian she recalled that Mr. Babcock's sister had married an Italian named Dino Santilli. The description fitted him in every respect, she said. Santilli lives at 630 Washington street, Gary.

When the Hammond police communicated with the Gary officers, Santilli was located without difficulty. Shortly before noon today Santilli came to Hammond and in company with Ed Babcock.

The description is as follows: Italian, about 28 years old; height, 5 feet, 6 inches; weight, 160 pounds; stout build; dark complexion; brown eyes; smooth shaven; black and bushy hair; freckles on face; blue and white striped shirt; brown suit; gray cap; low tan shoes; no collar.

Feeling between negroes and Italians of Chicago Heights has been running high for some time and deputy sheriffs were called out last week to patrol the streets. chicago-heights-chicago-heights-1920-08-.A20:
DAILY PAPER INVENTS STORY
W. R. Hearst's Herald-Examiner Manufactures Story of Chicago Heights Race Riot.

The many rumors, put afloat by various dailies in the latter part of last week, indicating that race riots were emminent in Chicago Heights, were found to be as baseless as they were vicious in their attempted explanation of the cause. One afternoon paper played up in bold type, "Her Military in Readiness, Fearing Desperate Wish Between Americans and Italians." Upon investigation by a special representative from the Whip office, this statement was found to be not only false, but seemingly born of an imaginary mind, having as its object the hope of stirring up race hatred.

As a matter of fact, the representatives assigned to investigate, found Chicago Heights as peaceful and contented as any other community. The Chief of Police, Thomas Stone, when asked about the call for troops characterized the statement as not only being false in its entirety, but a wild dream which had its inception in the brain of news monsters.

Dr. Chandler Makes Statement
Dr. Chandler makes statement

In an interview with Dr. E. H. Chandler, a chemist and leading colored citizen of Chicago Heights, residing at 22nd and Stewart Sts, he said, concerning the Examiner article this statement had no of fact, nor one scintilla of fact. On Dr. Chandler's behalf, the white and colored people of Chicago Heights have gotten along together in the most amiable manner. So far as colored people moving into colored and white districts is concerned, he said that there is no colored and white district in Chicago Heights', and that story is the outgrowth of the evil mind of the man who concocted it. He further stated that he knew of no hundreds of people leaving the city, and that motorcycle accident in which a colored man ran down and killed an Italian boy, had no connection with the present situation.

CHICAGO, Ill., Aug. 12—The riot reported by the daily newspapers between colored men and Italians at Chicago Heights is without foundation. There was a fight between a colored family and a few Italians when the latter went to the house of the Colored people looking for a Hungarian who was accused of having killed an Italian last week. The Hungarian had moved and rented to the Colored family.

There are about three thousand Colored men employed in the steel mills of Chicago Heights, where a strike has been in progress among the Italians and this has led to some strain and feeling which the news articles have magnified. Deputy Sheriff Sultan said there had been a clash.

The ugly riots reported at West Frankfort, Ill., and Denver, Colo., in which mobs are reported to have killed a number of people and destroyed thousands of dollars worth of property show the unceasing tendency of the American public toward mob violence and lynch law, said a prominent Colored official today. The government has sat supinely by while mobs have lynched Negroes and committed other atrocities upon us and may expect to reap a whirlwind from the seeds of discontent which its indifferent attitude has permitted to spring up.

TRAIN LEAP IS FATAL.
Colored Man Accused of Assault Suicide on Way to Jail.
Suicide on Way to Jail.
MIAMI, Fla., July 31.—The body of Herbert Brooks, who is alleged to have attacked a woman fifty-five years old in her home here yesterday, will be brought to Miami from Ormond, Fla., tonight for identification by the grand jury, which reconvenes Tuesday.
Brooks was killed at Ormond shortly after noon, when he sprang from the moving train on which he was being taken to Jacksonville to escape a mob of 1,200 infuriated white men, which surrounded the jail here Friday night and demanded the prisoner.
herbert-brooks-miami-1920-07-31.A3:
NEGRO SUSPECT
KILLED ON TRAIN
(By Associated Press.)
ni. Fla.. July 31—B

Miami, Fla., July 31—Herbert Brooks, arrested as a suspect in connection with the assault of an elderly white woman here yesterday, jumped from a moving train at Omond today and killed himself according to a telegram received this afternoon from Sheriff Monroe of St. Lucie county. The negro was being taken to Jacksonville for safe keeping, the sheriff of this county fearing mob violence.
herbert-brooks-miami-1920-07-31.A7:
FLORIDA NATIONAL GUARD
PRESERVES ORDER IN MIAM
Four Hundred Negroes From Bahamas Make Threats Following Death of Brooks. [By Associated Press]
[By Associated Press.]
[. FLA. August. 2]

MIAMI, FLA., August 2.—Fort men of the second separate Florida National Guard, heavily armed, are co-operating with the police tonight in preserving order in the negro settlement of Miami.

They were called out today after Mayor William Pruden Smith obtained the sanction of the Adjutant-General, because of a demonstration by more than 400 alien negroes from the Bahama Islands, following the arrival from Ormond, Fla., of the body of Herbert Brooks, who is alleged to have attacked a white woman here Friday. The negroes professed to believe Brooks had been killed by a mob and did not leap from the moving train on which he was being transported to Jacksonville Saturday for safe-keeping, and made threat of vengeance.

Brooks was a British subject and British Vice-Consul A. A. H. Hubbard demanded an autopsy. This was conducted by Dr. E. K. Jaudon, county physician, and revealed nothing of a sensational nature. The body was identified as Brooks' body. The woman had previously identified him as her assailant.

Troops patrolled the negro residence section last night.

Miami, Fla., Aug. 3. — State troops mobilized yesterday because of race trouble fears, were demobilized today after a negro who was killed in a jump from a train was put aboard a steamer for Nassau, Bahamas, for burial. The negro is charged with attacking an aged white woman and jumped to escape the officers. No disorders.

About 500 Bahama negroes here went on the war path yesterday when the body of Brooks arrived, the negroes not believing the report that the negro jumped from a train while being taken to Jacksonville for safe-keeping. They maintained he had been lynched, and feeling among them was high for a time.

Miami, Fin., Aug. 5—"If Chicago Negroes outnumbered twenty one, could stop race riots, Negroes equal to the whites, man to man, can an avenge a lynching," was the watchword of nearly one-fourth of the city's colored population yesterday when they organized, armed and threatened to wipe out white Miami. Only the arrival of the State militia prevented a pitched battle.

The trouble started over the death of Herbert Brooks, charged with assaulting a local white woman. While being taken to Jacksonville for safe keeping authorities say Brooks jumped off the train and was killed. Colored people say he was lynched. The arrival of a body here was the signal for the rise of the colorization, who met his body at the station, attended the funeral in crowds and buried it with great ceremony. Several whites were chased by angry persons from the colored section. Brooks was a West Indian and A. A. H. Hubbard. British vice counsel, demanded an autopsy which confirmed an accidental death. State troopers guard the city where the rides, Miami is the state of the worst cracker age. Northern white tourists were not allowed to have their colored chauffeurs drive them thru the city. HICKORY HITS.
Crops in this vicinity are at their best, with the corn made, and the cotton loaded with squares and the melon crop yielding bountifully, the farmers need to rejoice and send up their thanks to God.

The attendance at Sunday School on the 8th proved to be a record breaker. The adult class was at its best, being presided over by the pastor. The advanced class was well represented by the young men and ladies of the neighborhood, who discussed the lesson with much intelligence. It is with pleasure that I speak of the pastor., Rev. Henry Johnson in the highest terms. He has done much to uplift his people. He has progressed slowly but surely, as we know wonders can not be achieved at once; we must be satisfied to advance in improvement as we walk, step by step. The fruit best worth waiting for, often ripens the slowest. "Time and patience," says the Eastern poet, "change the mulberry leaf to satin."

The Ladies' Home Mission has been organized and it is proving a blessing to the people. The common life of every day with its cares, necessities and duties, afford ample opportunity for acquiring experience of the best kind. These sisters plan to entertain the public with a grand social soon for the benefit of human welfare.

Mrs. M. Golett and grand-daughter, little Alene Johnson are spending a few days at Hartshorn visiting friends. They are expected to arrive home in a few days.

Mrs. Laura Bird who has been very ill at her home is much improved of this writing.

Bahamans Back Up

MIAMI, Fla., Aug 13.—A riot was started here last Sunday by 400 Bahama Negroes who charged the local police with an unwarranted killing of one of their number, Herbert Brooks, who had been accused of assaulting a white woman. The Bahamans declare that Brooks was innocent of the charge and threatened to burn the city. Troops are in the city and are patrolling the Negro residence section.

Mayor writes The Governor Approving his Act in The Appointment of a Committee of Investigation
Durham.—Mayor Newsom, of Durham, has written Governor Bickett expressing approval of his plan for a thorough investigation into the shooting at Graham in which an innocent bystander was killed when members of the Durham machine gun company protecting three negroes in the jail at that place, fired on what they believed was a mob preparing to attack the jail, and asks to be notified as to whether arrangements have been made for counsel for the militiamen.

He assures the governor that Durham is solidly behind its military company and wishes to go the limit in protecting it from undeserved criticism.

JUSTIFY SOLDIERS' ACTION IN FIRING IN CAROLINA MOB
Special Committee Named to Investigate Alleged Assault on Jail Files Report. [By Associated Press.]
Files Report.
[By Associated Press.]
EIGH. N. C. August. 2

RALEIGH, N. C., August 20.—The committee appointed to investigate the alleged assault upon the Alamance County jail at Graham, and into the conduct of members of the Durham Machine Gun Company on the night of July 10, which resulted in the death of one man and the injuring of two others, today submitted its report to Governor Bickett justifying the action of the soldiers "in returning the fire, when the sentinels and jail were fired upon."

After reviewing the case in detail the report of the committee finds that "the conduct of the officers and of the men of the Machine Gun Company from the time they reached Graham and reported to the sheriff for duty until they were relieved on Tuesday morning, was in every respect most exemplary and soldierlike. The testimony satisfies us that none of the soldiers was under the influence of liquor and that there was no unseemly or ungentlemanly conduct on the part of any of them."

James Ray, who was killed near the jail, and Willis Phillips and Clem Bradshaw, who were wounded, were not members of any organized mob, the committee reports, but seemed to have been "innocent or curious onlookers."

The machine gunners were ordered to Graham to protect three negro prisoners who were lodged in the Alamance County jail in connection with an attack on a prominent white woman at that place.

Burlington, Sept. / 1—At the close of court last week the grand jury came to two important decisions. It was the duty of this body to investigate the recent killings in Alamance county. In doing so it found that James Ray came to his death by gun shots from the machine gunners, that there was no mob at the jail and that there was no provocation for the killing of Ray. Hoodlums' Bomb Does More Damage to White Than to Colored Homes.
The American reds who have for several months been destroying property owned in wealthy residential districts of our people are still at it. The latest attempt occurred Sunday night at 12:30 A. M., at 440 E. 48th St. The building is owned by a Mrs. Brinkley who still resides in the South and occupied by Mr. and Mrs. J. Jackson, who moved into the premises on Tuesday last.

Community Hires Watchman

Several weeks ago a number of property owners, fearing the "red" propaganda, employed J. D. Hardiman, an ex-soldier and retired regular army sergeant, 435 E. 48th St., as watchman. Hardiman, who is a property owner in the same neighborhood, made the following statement: "I was patrolling the alley so as to cover both 48th St. and 48th Pl., when a Ford touring car began cruising along 48th Pl. My suspicions were aroused, and I advanced toward the car. Evidently the occupants saw me, for an object was hurled from the car, but in the excitement and hurry not enough force was given it to land it on the entrance to the house, or even on the lawn. It fell on the parkway between the pavement and the road. The car speed up and I fired several shots. I was a good shot in the army and I believe I hit somebody."
mrs-jackson-chicago-1920-08-08.A3:
Only Slight Damage Done
The object hurled, which turned out to be a bomb, exploded without doing more damage than breaking out the windows in the houses along 48th Pl. More damage was done to the houses on the opposite side of the house occupied by whites than in the house for which the bomb was destined.

Authorities Inactive

The increased destruction in property is due to the inactivity of the law enforcement bodies in Cook county. It was no difficult task to convict William Bross Lloyd and his type of "reds" who has destroyed no property, but it seems to be beyond the jurisdiction of the Cook county prosecutor to ferret out and apprehend this particular brand of "reds," who are not only destroying property, but endangering lives.

CAROLINA GOVERNORS AT DAGGER POINTS

Raleigh, N. C., Aug. 11—At the instance W. S. Braswell, sheriff of Anson County, Gov. Bickett has issued a requisition on the governor of South Carolina demanding the surrender of three white men who kidnapped several colored men a few days ago and took them back to South Carolina. A requisition had been made for the colored men by the South Carolina authorities, but Gov. Bickett declared that the offenses were so trivial that he would not honor the requisitions. Thereupon, W. D. Mayfield, James Breeding, and Henry B. Sandifer, white, crossed the state line from South Carolina, and kidnapped the men alleged to be wanted. The action on the part of the South Carolina officials has caused a tense and bitter feeling between the two Carolinas.

Police Chief, Fatally Shot, Kills Assailant
Third Man Seriously Wounded in Row at North Carolina Carnival Dance
WINSTON-SALEM, N. C., Aug. 22. Chief of Police Matthews of Walnut Cove, N. C., and Walter Martin, of Madison, are dead, and a negro whose name has not been ascertained is seriously wounded, as the result of a battle in the road near Walnut Cove to-day between a sheriff's posse and three Madison, N. C., escaping prisoners.

The shooting was the result of a row at a carnival dance, hall at which observers assert the negro insisted on dancing with white girls. A disturbance started and several Madison men, including Martin and the negro, were arrested. On the way to the Mayor's office they escaped in an automobile.

Chief Matthews formed one of a posse summoned to pursue the fleeing prisoners and they were overtaken near Walnut Cove. A summons to surrender met with a fusillade, and Matthews was shot through the stomach. Crumpled in his seat, he shot and killed Walter Martin, while the negro escaped. The negro was trailed for a couple of miles by blood but was lost in a swamp. Bloodhounds have been ordered to the scene.

A total of 76 rattlesnakes, varying in length from eight inches to three feet, were killed the other day by Frank Wright, an employee of the Carolina Dray company, at an old saw mill in the vicinity of Ashevill. The snakes were discovered under a partly rotten lag.

Davidson county Democrats, have nominated a woman for register of deeds, thereby officially acknowledging the entry of women into politics. The nominee is Mrs. Mattie Cecil Young, wife of an ex-mayor of Lexington, and the nomination was made by acclamation and amid continued applause.

—Wounded by a pistol bullet from a weapon in the hands of a playmate, William Jones, eight years old, of Durham, died at a local hospital a few days ago. —Claud Bowles, an ex-soldier, last Sunday afternoon shot and killed Thelbert Ellis, a prosperous young farmer of Person county, who wooed and married the girl he loved. The shooting took place near the home of the girl's parent's near the Durham-Person county line. Posses are searching for Bowles.

—One sixth of the entire membership of the Junior Order U. A. M. is found in North Carolina, according to a recent report of the State secretary of the order. With a membership of more than 52,000 in about 500 councils, North Carolina is second only to Pennsylvania in the number of members included in the order.

—Hundreds of men and women from all parts of North Carolina are attending the North Carolina Farmers' and Farm Women's Convention being held at Raleigh this week. The program of the convention embraces discussion and demonstration of nearly every subject that the farmers of the State and theri wives will be interested in.

—After wrapping his false teeth carefully in a handkerchief, W. L. Ferrell, veteran of both the Spanish-American war and the world war, committed suicide in a Raleigh park a few days ago, slashing his throat with a razor. He was 40 years old. Ill health is believed to have been the reason for the rash act.

Marvin Holliday of Greensboro went to the home of Thomas Monroe, 18 years old several days ago, called him to the door, and fired four shots at him, none of which took effect. He went ashore, put on his clothes, and made a search which ended with the discovery of a new-born babe only a few hours old, abandoned in the woods. The finder adopted the child, and is making a quiet investigation for its parents.

Mrs. Leak received injuries from which her death resulted a few hours later at a local hospital. She was 71 years old.

were held, one at Durham, and the other at Graham, where citizens of the latter city were examined in the course of the investigation.

The stone was a smooth rock which McKay has picked up at the seashore. A few days ago, the darky entered the drug store, accompanied by his spouse, and, as McKay thought, to ask for his $35 back. Instead, Baggott and his wife both declared that the "charmed" stone had greatly benefitted Mrs. Baggott, and they informed the astonished McKay that they would not take $50 for the rock.

—As the result of a battle between a sheriff's posse and three escaping negro prisoners near Walnut Cove, in Forsyth county last Sunday, chief of police Matthews of Walnut Cove, and a white man by the name of Martin, are dead, and an unknown Negro is seriously wounded. The shooting was the result of a quarrel at a carnival dance hall, when one of the negroes present insisted on dancing with white show girls. Martin, the negro, and one Hawkins, white, were placed under arrest, but on their way to the mayor's office they escaped and fled in a waiting automobile. A posse was formed, which pursued and overtook the trio near Walnut Cove. A summons to surrender met with a fusillade of shots, in the course of which Matthews and Martin were killed. The negro, though wounded, made his escape. Hawkins was later recaptured, and lodged in jail.

A determined effort is being made by business men of New Bern to dissuade the Federal government from moving the yards of the Newport Shipbuilding company at that city. A short time ago the government gave orders to this shipyard to build twelve concrete ships at a cost of $5,000,000, some of the ships to draw as much as 12 feet of water. The bar in New Bern harbor is nine feet under water at high tide, and manager Bedell of the yards reported to Federal officials that the vessels of deeper draft must be built at other yards. The United States shipping board concluded on the basis of this report that it would be best to build all the ships elsewhere, and that it would abandon and dismantle the New Bern yards, which would be a serious blow to the latter city. New Bern now offers to dredge the bar to a depth of 12 or more feet, provided assurance is given that the yards will not be moved.

Winston-Salem, N. C., Aug. 26. —Outsiders who objected to color- and white people dancing to-theater at a carnival dance hall, interfered last night with fateful peace. Chief of police Matthews, and Walter Martin, both white, are dead as a result of the fight between a gang of sheriffs and the dancers. When the sheriff approached the dance, he arrested one of the colored men found dancing with a posse, Matthew and Matthews and a posse pursued them. When the dancers were ordered to surrender, they replied with a fusilade of bullets, killing the sheriff and just before he fell, he shot Martin who was one of the white dancers. The colored men, the sheriff fell. Although bloodbounds have been used he was not retaken.
